subject: FinVista POC: workload intake & success guardrails
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Leah Ortiz <leah.ortiz@finvista.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-10T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: FinVista POC: workload intake & success guardrails

Hi Leah — great conversation earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before kickoff.

Call highlights (from our side):
- FinVista wants a 3-week POC to validate production latency and cost at your peak traffic patterns.
- Primary workload: customer-facing recommendation endpoint with short conversational prompts and occasional long-context batch reranks.
- Key concerns: burst-handling across marketing campaigns, predictable tail latency, and end-to-end observability.

Proposed success guardrails (we can refine):
1) Latency: P50 < 120ms, P95 < 450ms for 512-token responses under baseline traffic.
2) Throughput: sustain 120 RPS steady-state with 4,000 concurrent KV-cache contexts (worst-case).
3) Error budget: < 0.5% 5xx rate during business hours.
4) Cost signal: token cost per 1k responses <= $X (we'll finalize once we have token distribution).
5) Functional: sample prompts pass your 10 canonical success prompts with equivalent output quality (Leah to share).

What we need from you to finalize the plan:
- Traffic sample (CSV) showing RPS, average/95th token lengths, concurrency and typical burst windows (5-min granularity is fine).
- A prioritized list of the 10 success prompts and expected semantic checks.
- Any network/firewall constraints and expected start date for test traffic.

Next steps (owners and timeline):
- Leah: send traffic sample + success prompts by EOD Mon, Apr 12.
- Ben: will prepare an intake spreadsheet for detailed RPS/token mapping and initial infra sizing (ETA Wed Apr 14).
- Jonas: will own the monitoring/trace hooks and reporting dashboard for the POC.
- Tessa: coordinate kickoff and scoping call once we receive traffic sample; target POC start week of Apr 19.

Attachments: finvista-poc-requirements.xlsx (skeleton POC template)

Thanks — excited to get this moving.

—
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(t) 415-555-0123
Tessa.Morgan@redwood.ai

From: Leah Ortiz <leah.ortiz@finvista.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@finvista.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinVista POC: workload intake & success guardrails

Thanks Tessa — appreciated the write-up. Attaching the initial traffic export and a short doc with the 10 priority prompts. High-level notes from our side:
- Baseline: 40 RPS steady (weekdays, 9–17 PT).
- Campaign bursts: up to 400 RPS sustained for 8–12 minutes during promotional pushes (approx twice per week).
- Typical response token lengths: median 48 tokens, mean 62, 95th percentile ~320.
- Concurrency: typical active sessions ~600, peaks near 3,200 during campaigns.

Files attached: api-traffic-sample-202703.csv, finvista-priority-prompts.txt

Questions:
- Do you recommend we include the long-context reranks in the first phase or stage them? Those jobs are batch and can be delayed if it complicates infra sizing.
- We have an internal SSO firewall; we'll need IP ranges for the POC endpoints.

We'll try to get the complete samples to you by EOD Mon.

—
Leah Ortiz
Director of ML Engineering | FinVista
leah.ortiz@finvista.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Leah Ortiz <leah.ortiz@finvista.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11T11:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinVista POC: workload intake & success guardrails

Leah — thanks for the sample and stats, that helps a lot. Quick technical intake questions so we can size and recommend config:

1) Traffic shape: can you confirm whether the campaign bursts are uniform across users or concentrated on a small subset of endpoints (i.e., are bursts targeted to a few routes or broadly across many)?
2) Token distribution: is the 95th (~320) token length mostly for the long-context rerank jobs or interactive sessions?
3) Reranks: are those executed synchronously on the tail of an interactive request or asynchronously as a separate batch pipeline? If async, what's the typical batch size and acceptable latency window?
4) Auth: do you want us to host a dedicated VPC endpoint for the POC or can you use our hosted endpoints with IP allowlist?

Initial sizing notes (very rough):
- For 40 RPS steady + 400 RPS bursts: recommend a dedicated pool with burst routing and autoscale to handle <= 500 RPS safely; add KV-prefill for session contexts to reduce cold-start overhead.
- For 95th token lengths ~320: we'll prioritize memory-friendly quantization and enable continuous batching for steady-state to hit P50 targets.

I'll assemble a more precise config once we get the per-route RPS CSV and a small sample payload set (~100 requests) so we can run a microbenchmark.

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Leah Ortiz <leah.ortiz@finvista.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@finvista.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T08:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinVista POC: workload intake & success guardrails

Ben — answers inline below (quoted for clarity):

> 1) Traffic shape: are bursts concentrated on a few routes?
Most bursts are on the recommendation endpoint (/api/recs) triggered by marketing campaigns. Other endpoints see a small uplift but are relatively stable.

> 2) Token distribution: is the 95th (~320) token length mostly for the long-context rerank jobs or interactive sessions?
The 95th is mostly interactive sessions that include long product descriptions; reranks are typically longer (median ~900 tokens) but run as separate batch jobs.

> 3) Reranks: are those executed synchronously or asynchronously? If async, batch size and latency window?
Reranks are async—batched nightly for most flows but for a couple of high-priority flows we run near-real-time batches (~50 items) with an SLA of 2 minutes.

> 4) Auth: dedicated VPC endpoint or hosted with allowlist?
We prefer using Redwood hosted endpoints behind an IP allowlist for speed of setup. We'll provide the allowlist of our egress IPs.

Attaching a small payload sample (100 requests) and the CSV. Please confirm if the CSV schema is ok.

Attachments: api-traffic-sample-202703.csv, finvista-payload-examples.json (stub)

Thanks — aiming to have everything in place so you can begin the microbench week of Apr 19.

—
Leah Ortiz
Director of ML Engineering | FinVista

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Leah Ortiz <leah.ortiz@finwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinVista POC: workload intake & success guardrails

Great — thanks everyone. Summary and confirmed plan: 
- Intake accepted: traffic CSV and 100 request payloads received.
- Scope for Phase 1 (week of Apr 19): microbench + live smoke tests focusing on /api/recs (steady 40 RPS, targeted campaign bursts up to 400 RPS).
- Phase 2 (if Phase 1 passes guardrails): expand to near-real-time rerank batches (50 items, SLA 2m) and validate cost signalling.

Owners and dates:
- Tessa (AE): commercial check-in and procurement path; coordinate DS/POC kickoff by Apr 19.
- Ben (SE): infra config and initial benchmarks (deliverable Apr 21).
- Jonas (Platform): observability dashboard and alerting (deliverable Apr 23).
- Leah (FinVista): finalize IP allowlist and confirm any data redaction rules (deliverable Apr 16).

Immediate asks for FinVista: please confirm the CSV schema is correct (Ben will reply with any tweaks) and share the IP list. We'll aim to run the microbench on Apr 20 if infra is green.

I'll open a HubSpot deal note and a shared Drive folder with the runbooks and test results.

Thanks — looking forward to kickoff.

—
